authority: User-requested roadmap refinement; no execution admission

lessons.title: Classify financial function separately from mechanism, claim and interface
lessons.positive: Classify a scoped component with multiple financial functions and independent trust/execution facets; map FIN identifiers to existing F1–F6/P and DA targets.
lessons.negative: Reject brand-only labels, an ERC number treated as an economic product, or taxonomy roots automatically becoming Core constructors.

lessons.title: Pin sources, revisions and evidence levels
lessons.positive: Keep publication, revision, observation window, deployment and verification dates distinct; record spec, code, deployment, adoption and security evidence independently.
lessons.negative: Reject code availability as deployed-bytecode identity, a recent paper as current measurements, or an unverified live composition.

lessons.title: Use nominal financial quantities
lessons.positive: Represent asset identity, shares, principal, accrued interest, fees, request quantity and time units distinctly; conversions name scale, rounding and policy.
lessons.negative: Reject mixed-asset arithmetic, debt erased by zero cash payoff, or implicit shares-to-assets conversion.

lessons.title: Distinguish four valuation purposes
lessons.positive: Accounting, realizable redemption, market and stressed-liquidation values each carry source, time, validity, units and a selected policy.
lessons.negative: Reject donation-derived borrowing capacity, stale/corrected NAV as current cash, and accounting value used as exit liquidity without the additional assumption.

lessons.title: Separate conversion, preview, limit, authorization and execution
lessons.positive: Cover all four ERC-4626 preview directions, method-specific fee/rounding inequalities and max limits; actual signed min-net/max-gross constraints govern execution.
lessons.negative: Reject nonzero preview as permission, a preview as a guaranteed future quote, and affected ERC-7540 async previews that succeed.

lessons.title: Carry requests and residual entitlements
lessons.positive: Pending→Claimable→Claimed preserves controller, locked quantity, partial fulfillment and unfilled rights. A cancel route needs a pinned explicit extension/policy.
lessons.negative: Reject double claim/cancel payout, deleted pending rights at work exhaustion, and queued redemption represented as available money.

lessons.title: Preserve liabilities, accrual and loss allocation
lessons.positive: For the explicit interest-first policy, P100/I10 paid7 leaves P100/I3; time and allocation rules are separate from ACTUS normative fields. NAM19 and refinance preserve debt identity.
lessons.negative: Reject repeated accrual over one interval, unsigned capitalization, full debt deletion after partial liquidation, or a monotone share-price invariant that excludes allowed loss.

lessons.title: Compare all ordered material effects
lessons.positive: Trace fees, change, transfer deltas, callbacks, rebases, donations, strategy losses and intermediate shared-state observations; failed atomic actions roll back all legs.
lessons.negative: Reject ABI-only compatibility, copied expected outputs, net-only accounting that hides a harmful intermediate call, and same-block repayment substituted for one atomic transaction.

lessons.title: Bind complete outcome authority
lessons.positive: Separate intent, authority, proposal, execution and receipt; bind cumulative gross spend, net receipt, recipients, new liabilities, expiry and partial-fill residuals to canonical signed display.
lessons.negative: Reject refund-reset budgets, exact-output overdelivery when equality is required, hidden liabilities, and a compromised solver expanding a signing request.

lessons.title: State economic and external assumptions
lessons.positive: Preserve Werner’s atomic/non-atomic distinction and Zhou’s dependency/threat layers; trace returns to their payer and state oracle, custody, liquidity, legal and finality assumptions.
lessons.negative: Reject proof-valid price authentication as economic truth, a wrapper as a source of yield, flash liquidity as the root vulnerability, or token ownership as legal enforceability.

lessons.title: Bound composition without inventing atomicity
lessons.positive: Five operators preserve global work, authority, obligations and shared collateral; separate local success, foreign settlement and solver reimbursement with bounded recovery and unavailable outcomes.
lessons.negative: Reject resetting work at split/join, treating two wrappers as independent reserves, or a local intent proof as foreign finality. Witness unavailability differs from invalidity.

lessons.title: Bind interface revisions and implementation behavior
lessons.positive: Pin spec revision, component version, adapter traits and material upgrade authority. ERC-7575 external shares differ from entry points; ERC-7683 May 2026 resolver/payment/assumption semantics differ from old settler drafts.
lessons.negative: Reject automatic substitutability, old Across interfaces as current ERC-7683 conformance, unsupported ERC-7887 cancellation, or ERC-7943 transfer checks as universal legal compliance.

lessons.title: Prove the complete native acceptance boundary
lessons.positive: Keep F0→path freeze→F0a→independent non-loan fixtures→all F1 controls→F2→atomic F3. Verify serialized proofs, carried accumulators and the actual outer final pairing under pinned deployment context.
lessons.negative: Reject host booleans, transcript-only success, circular loan-derived admission fixtures, unchecked finalizers and retrying the failed k17 encoding without a reviewed changed hypothesis.

lessons.title: Require nonvacuous mechanized correspondence
lessons.positive: Prove explicit elaboration/evaluator/compiler/native/ledger domains and all four mandatory claims; include feasible positive transitions and a deliberately falsified claim.
lessons.negative: Reject an always-reject compiler, finite tests as universal proofs, optional genesis/admin checks and inherited proof status after extending the semantic domain.

lessons.title: Attach real network evidence to financial milestones
lessons.positive: Use Preview alone; retain actual transaction ID, canonical finality, deployment/profile and independent full effect comparison; report submitted IDs and failures in the conversation.
lessons.negative: Reject synthetic transport as settlement, indexer inclusion as canonical finality, hello-world as financial acceptance, and two public samples closing all required financial behavior.

lessons.title: Deliver a usable and independently reproducible release
lessons.positive: Introduce check/format/simulate and signed display with their owning capabilities; retain exact G01–G24, two clean builders, two non-toy pilots against the audited Compact-library baseline, licensing and a separate confidential-profile leakage theorem.
lessons.negative: Reject a final-week mock UX demonstration, retained-receipt verification described as a fresh transaction, or an assurance claim missing a named trusted dependency.

lessons.title: Keep execution focused on demonstrated capability
lessons.positive: Reuse accepted atomic work and existing task/command records. Each slice ends with a real capability demonstration, decisive probe or concrete resolved blocker. Keep one primary capability and one writer per shared file.
lessons.negative: Reject repeated packet work as progress, a third same-defect correction without reproducer/changed approach, blanket campaign gates for routine edits, and a new loop or dashboard to enforce these instructions.

lessons.title: Retain the entire financial denominator
lessons.positive: Retain all original inventories plus TX01–12/VX01–06 modeled regressions. Account for all 24 modern cases as scoped comparative evidence and resolve three uncovered taxonomy leaves with source-defined fixtures before coverage claims.
lessons.negative: Reject replacing 72 historical rows with 24 newer cases, taxonomy edges as conformance, dropped difficult ACTUS fields, or increasing resources silently when added obligations exceed the existing allocation.

modeledRegressions.title: TX01
modeledRegressions.positive: A vault with 100 assets and 80 shares issues 20 shares for a 25-asset deposit under an explicitly selected floor policy.
modeledRegressions.negative: Asset/share unit substitution; wrong rounding direction; zero-supply case that divides by zero; donation changes entitlement unexpectedly.
modeledRegressions.claimScope: Hypothetical bounded model; not a reproduced incident or deployed protocol conformance.

modeledRegressions.title: TX02
modeledRegressions.positive: Debt is principal 100, accrued interest 10. Payment 7 under interest-first allocation leaves principal 100 and interest 3.
modeledRegressions.negative: Marking the position closed, erasing residual interest, or silently capitalizing it without liability authority.
modeledRegressions.claimScope: Hypothetical bounded model; not a reproduced incident or deployed protocol conformance.

modeledRegressions.title: TX03
modeledRegressions.positive: Simple interest 100 × 10/100 × 30/360 equals 5 before the selected final rounding; accrue once over that declared interval.
modeledRegressions.negative: Substituting block count for elapsed contractual time, applying the same interval twice, or moving across a rate kink using the wrong pre/post utilization.
modeledRegressions.claimScope: Hypothetical bounded model; not a reproduced incident or deployed protocol conformance.

modeledRegressions.title: TX04
modeledRegressions.positive: Flash principal 100 plus fee 1 is repaid within one admitted atomic operation; all effects bind to that operation.
modeledRegressions.negative: Repay only 100; repay 101 in a later transaction in the same block; fail the final leg after earlier tentative transfers.
modeledRegressions.claimScope: Hypothetical bounded model; not a reproduced incident or deployed protocol conformance.

modeledRegressions.title: TX05
modeledRegressions.positive: With outstanding debt 100 and an illustrative 50% close limit, authorized partial liquidation repays 40 and preserves debt 60, with separately calculated collateral/bonus.
modeledRegressions.negative: Repay 60 despite the limit; seize using a stale/wrong-unit price; erase shortfall or remaining collateral rights.
modeledRegressions.claimScope: Hypothetical bounded model; not a reproduced incident or deployed protocol conformance.

modeledRegressions.title: TX06
modeledRegressions.positive: A redemption request moves Pending → Claimable → Claimed with exact remaining shares, controller and entitlement.
modeledRegressions.negative: Illiquidity erases the request; double claim; unauthorized cancellation; exhausted work deletes a surviving right.
modeledRegressions.claimScope: Hypothetical bounded model; not a reproduced incident or deployed protocol conformance.

modeledRegressions.title: TX07
modeledRegressions.positive: Two calls on shared reserves compose under declared observation order and conflict rules.
modeledRegressions.negative: Independent local checks reuse the same pre-state, accept incompatible effects, or inspect an intermediate state through a callback.
modeledRegressions.claimScope: Hypothetical bounded model; not a reproduced incident or deployed protocol conformance.

modeledRegressions.title: TX08
modeledRegressions.positive: A signed observation has the selected feed, units, domain, freshness and sequence.
modeledRegressions.negative: A validly signed but manipulable spot price is treated as a guarantee of economic truth. The model must expose the assumption and the attack can remain economically possible.
modeledRegressions.claimScope: Hypothetical bounded model; not a reproduced incident or deployed protocol conformance.

modeledRegressions.title: TX09
modeledRegressions.positive: One outcome authorization accumulates gross spending, fees and net delivery across partial fills.
modeledRegressions.negative: Refund resets gross allowance; reordered fills spend the same residual record; same endpoint balance hides an extra intermediate call or liability.
modeledRegressions.claimScope: Hypothetical bounded model; not a reproduced incident or deployed protocol conformance.

modeledRegressions.title: TX10
modeledRegressions.positive: A parameter update or loss allocation uses the bound authorized version and preserves existing duties.
modeledRegressions.negative: New governance settings retroactively reinterpret a signed obligation; temporary borrowed voting power is treated as durable consent; compromised custody is assumed impossible.
modeledRegressions.claimScope: Hypothetical bounded model; not a reproduced incident or deployed protocol conformance.

modeledRegressions.title: TX11
modeledRegressions.positive: A bounded strategy withdraws a specified upstream claim, accounts for fees/slippage and deposits the authorized amount downstream.
modeledRegressions.negative: Partial leg success is reported as atomic success; recursive strategy expansion exceeds bounds; zero-liquidation lending is misclassified as guaranteed principal preservation.
modeledRegressions.claimScope: Hypothetical bounded model; not a reproduced incident or deployed protocol conformance.

modeledRegressions.title: TX12
modeledRegressions.positive: A foreign redemption/message creates a bounded pending state and requires the selected authenticated settlement observation before discharge.
modeledRegressions.negative: A local proof or bridge message is treated as proof of foreign finality, reserve custody or actual payment; unavailable witness is equated to invalid commitment.
modeledRegressions.claimScope: Hypothetical bounded model; not a reproduced incident or deployed protocol conformance.

modeledRegressions.title: VX01: donation and minimum shares
modeledRegressions.positive: In a naive model, 1 share backed by 1 asset plus a donation of 100 gives 101 assets/share. A later 100-asset deposit would mint floor(100/101)=0; an intent requiring at least 1 share rejects before accepted effects.
modeledRegressions.negative: Accept assets while satisfying a forged minimum-share claim, or assert a mitigation is safe for every future deposit sequence after one test.
modeledRegressions.claimScope: Hypothetical bounded model; not a reproduced incident or deployed protocol conformance.

modeledRegressions.title: VX02: accounting versus collateral value
modeledRegressions.positive: A donation changes accounting assets/share from 100/100 to 200/100. An explicitly selected external valuation/cap policy independently determines allowable debt.
modeledRegressions.negative: Convert the doubled ratio directly into twice the debt allowance without the signed/pinned collateral policy. Donation cost remains part of any profitability analysis.
modeledRegressions.claimScope: Hypothetical bounded model; not a reproduced incident or deployed protocol conformance.

modeledRegressions.title: VX03: preview, limit and execution
modeledRegressions.positive: A hypothetical preview is 10 shares while the current deposit limit is zero: query results can coexist, but the deposit rejects under the selected limit policy. Same-state preview inequalities follow the method's contract.
modeledRegressions.negative: Treat a nonzero preview as permission or liquidity guarantee; use an earlier preview as a future exact quote.
modeledRegressions.claimScope: Hypothetical bounded model; not a reproduced incident or deployed protocol conformance.

modeledRegressions.title: VX04: asynchronous claim and race
modeledRegressions.positive: A request preserves owner/controller and remaining amount through partial fulfillment and claim. Unsupported preview paths reject; any cancellation policy must specify when the claim wins or cancels.
modeledRegressions.negative: Duplicate claim/cancel payout, loss of unfilled entitlement, or unapproved transfer of a pending right.
modeledRegressions.claimScope: Hypothetical bounded model; not a reproduced incident or deployed protocol conformance.

modeledRegressions.title: VX05: repeated rounding and loss
modeledRegressions.positive: A finite sequence records every rounding remainder, fee and injected strategy loss and preserves the selected quantitative invariant.
modeledRegressions.negative: A local round-trip passes while repeated operations inflate a downstream ratio or a “monotone share price” invariant ignores allowed losses.
modeledRegressions.claimScope: Hypothetical bounded model; not a reproduced incident or deployed protocol conformance.

modeledRegressions.title: VX06: nested exposure and privileges
modeledRegressions.positive: Two allocation paths referencing one underlying position remain traceable to that shared exposure; material oracle/adapter/cap changes bind a versioned authority rule.
modeledRegressions.negative: Count two wrappers as independently backed reserves, restore gross spending by netting, or reinterpret signed debt after an unbound upgrade.
modeledRegressions.claimScope: Hypothetical bounded model; not a reproduced incident or deployed protocol conformance.
